The investigation is solved, but the teacher needs a reliable witness record. Read your Alibi review note. Ask your partner which clock or record they used and whether a sound proves a person was present. Explain one apparent contradiction using both notes. Submit the original claim, the evidence and your correction; mark anything you cannot yet verify. Useful phrases: "Which clock did you use?" "That could mean..." "The evidence shows..."

Visitors have heard a damaging rumor. Read your Rumor repair note. Discuss with your partner which claims are facts and which are guesses. Agree on a calm public update that explains one checked fact, corrects one unsupported claim and invites a question. Submit your agreed message and explain what your partner changed. Useful phrases: "We can confirm..." "We cannot be sure about..." "Let's change that sentence because..."

chapters.title: The Haunted Celebration
chapters.intro: The hotel hall is ready. Before the celebration, a lantern disappears and a ghostly sound comes from the park. A strange invitation says there are special guests. Investigate the sound, recover the lantern and find out who the surprise is for.
chapters.recap: Last time: you checked the latest festival plan and proposed a safe celebration in the hotel hall.
chapters.ending: The lantern is recovered. The "ghost" was wind through a torn paper lantern, and the surprise is a welcome for the new neighbors. Your explanation and welcome proposal are ready. The town can celebrate together!

roleClues.baker: The missing lantern was beside the food boxes. The driver moved the boxes past the park.

title: Castanyada: Witness Investigations
finale: The town celebrates together. You recovered the chestnuts, checked the stories, made a safe festival plan and welcomed the new neighbors. Your investigations helped everyone belong. Happy Castanyada!

roles.name: Café baker
roles.clue: No blue box came to the café.

roles.name: Shopkeeper
roles.clue: A blue box left the shop at 9:00.

roles.name: Driver
roles.clue: I carried a blue box. I left it near the water.

roles.name: Hotel receptionist
roles.card: You work at the hotel desk.
roles.clue: No box came to the hotel.

roles.name: Festival planner
roles.clue: The only water in town is the pond in the park.

chapters.title: The Missing Chestnuts
chapters.intro: The chestnuts are gone. Ask your classmates. Each of you knows something different. Before each conclusion, ask a witness about this question and compare their private evidence with yours in your journal.
chapters.recap: Last time: the big box of chestnuts disappeared. You are still looking for it.
chapters.ending: Two people have a key: the shopkeeper and the planner. But the lock is open and the box is empty! Who took the chestnuts?

objectives.text: Where is the blue box?

rewards.baker: The café needs 20 chestnuts. That is half of the box.
rewards.shopkeeper: I packed 40 chestnuts in the box.
rewards.driver: The ride from the shop to the park takes 30 minutes.
rewards.receptionist: A man in a green coat asked me about the park at 9:15.
rewards.planner: The party starts at 6:00. We need the chestnuts before 5:00.

objectives.text: What time did the box get to the park?

rewards.baker: There is no key at the café.
rewards.shopkeeper: I have one key. It is on my belt.
rewards.driver: I never have a key. I only carry the box.
rewards.receptionist: There is no key at the hotel.
rewards.planner: I have one key. The other key is in the shop.

objectives.text: How many people have a key?

rewards.baker: Delivery audit: I ordered paper lanterns, not another box of food. Fair shares: the cafe needs 20 of the 40 chestnuts to roast for guests.
rewards.shopkeeper: Delivery audit: a second parcel had a moon label, not the blue box label. Fair shares: ten children will arrive and each wants one chestnut.
rewards.driver: Delivery audit: I left the moon parcel at the hotel desk at 10:00. Fair shares: I can carry one tray of ten chestnuts at a time.
rewards.receptionist: Delivery audit: the moon parcel contains folded paper and candles. Fair shares: ten new neighbors have been invited to the hotel.
rewards.planner: Delivery audit: the moon parcel is for festival decorations. Fair shares: there are 40 chestnuts in total; every guest should get a fair share.

objectives.text: What does the note on the hotel door say?
What is on the lock?
How many chestnuts were in the box?
Write 2 sentences. Who do you think has the chestnuts? Why?

The town needs to know whether a second delivery is connected to the missing chestnuts. Read your Delivery audit note. Interview your assigned partner in English: What arrived? Where did it go? When? Ask one follow-up question. Compare your evidence and write a short delivery record with both findings and anything still uncertain. Useful phrases: "What did you see?" "How do you know?" "So, do we agree that...?"

Help the festival committee plan a fair distribution. Read your Fair shares note and ask your partner about their needs. Suggest two ways to share the 40 chestnuts, explain a problem with each, and agree on a plan that uses no more than 40. Write the allocations, one reason and your partner's contribution. Useful phrases: "We need... because..." "What if we...?" "Could we agree on...?"

discoveries.text: A note on the hotel door: "The chestnuts are safe. Do not worry."
A small blue lock with a star on it, on the grass.

reveals.text: News: a neighbor saw a person in a green coat near the park at 9:20.
News: somebody heard a lock click in the park.

chapters.title: Conflicting Stories
chapters.intro: Now people tell different stories. Somebody in this class took the chestnuts! Ask questions. Who is lying? Before each conclusion, ask a witness about this question and compare their private evidence with yours in your journal.
chapters.recap: Last time: the box was in the park, and the lock was open. You are looking for who opened it.
chapters.ending: You found the thief. But why did they take the chestnuts?

thieves.card: You took the chestnuts. Tell nobody! If a classmate asks, say you are innocent. Your classmates saw how you look, so be careful.
thieves.story: At 9:25 I was at the hotel desk.

roleClues.baker: At 9:20 somebody ran past the café. {hat}
roleClues.shopkeeper: At 9:10 somebody came to my shop. {coat} {glasses}
roleClues.driver: At 9:30 somebody ran into the park. {hair}
roleClues.receptionist: The hotel phone rang at 9:25. Nobody answered.
roleClues.planner: My key was in my bag. Somebody moved my bag at 9:00.

objectives.text: Who is the shopkeeper? Type their name.

rewards.baker: At 9:15 the café was empty. Nobody came.
rewards.shopkeeper: At 9:05 I went to the bank. The shop door was open.
rewards.driver: At 9:25 I was in my truck near the hotel. Nobody went in.
rewards.receptionist: At 9:25 the hotel was closed. Nobody was at the desk.
rewards.planner: At 9:20 I was in the square with the band.

objectives.text: Who is the planner? Type their name.
Who took the chestnuts? Type their name.

rewards.baker: Alibi review: the cafe clock was five minutes slow. Rumor repair: somebody told visitors that everyone in town steals things; that is unfair.
rewards.shopkeeper: Alibi review: my receipt is stamped 9:05 by the shop clock, which was correct. Rumor repair: an open door alone does not prove who entered.
rewards.driver: Alibi review: the truck clock agreed with the shop clock. Rumor repair: I saw someone running, but I did not see what was in their bag.
rewards.receptionist: Alibi review: the hotel bell rings automatically at 9:25, even if nobody is at the desk. Rumor repair: a ringing bell does not prove a receptionist was there.
rewards.planner: Alibi review: my rehearsal list records the band in the square at 9:20. Rumor repair: name a fact, explain your evidence, and avoid blaming people for things you cannot prove.

objectives.text: Write 2 sentences. How do you know who took the chestnuts?

The investigation is solved, but the teacher needs a reliable witness record. Read your Alibi review note. Ask your partner which clock or record they used and whether a sound proves a person was present. Explain one apparent contradiction using both notes. Submit the original claim, the evidence and your correction; mark anything you cannot yet verify. Useful phrases: "Which clock did you use?" "That could mean..." "The evidence shows..."

Visitors have heard a damaging rumor. Read your Rumor repair note. Discuss with your partner which claims are facts and which are guesses. Agree on a calm public update that explains one checked fact, corrects one unsupported claim and invites a question. Submit your agreed message and explain what your partner changed. Useful phrases: "We can confirm..." "We cannot be sure about..." "Let's change that sentence because..."

reveals.text: News: the shop door was open at 9:05.
News: the hotel phone rang at 9:25.

chapters.title: The Hotel Cellar
chapters.intro: It is late afternoon. You know who took the chestnuts. Find them before the party starts at 6:00! Before each conclusion, ask a witness about this question and compare their private evidence with yours in your journal.
chapters.recap: Last time: you found the thief. The chestnuts are still hidden somewhere.
chapters.ending: The chestnuts are safe! The thief wanted a surprise party and says sorry. But the festival plan is missing. Can the town prepare a safe celebration in time?

thieves.label: Your plan
thieves.card: You hid the chestnuts in the hotel cellar, for a surprise party. Give small hints. Never say the answers!
thieves.story: Help the class with hints, but do not tell them where the chestnuts are.

roleClues.baker: I smell hot chestnuts near the hotel.
roleClues.shopkeeper: At 9:00 somebody bought wood and matches. You need fire to roast chestnuts.
roleClues.driver: At 9:40 I carried a heavy bag to the hotel.
roleClues.receptionist: The cellar door at the hotel is old and locked. It has a four-number code.
roleClues.planner: The party starts at 6:00. The chestnuts must be ready before then.

objectives.text: Where did the thief hide the chestnuts?

rewards.baker: One number of the code is 4. It is the number of my oven.
rewards.shopkeeper: One number of the code is 1. It is the number of doors in my shop.
rewards.driver: One number of the code is 7. It is the number of my truck.
rewards.receptionist: One number of the code is 3. It is the number of the hotel key.
rewards.planner: Read the numbers in this order: driver, baker, receptionist, shopkeeper.

objectives.text: What is the code of the cellar door? Type the four numbers.

rewards.baker: In the cellar there is a note. It says: "I wanted a surprise..."
rewards.shopkeeper: The note says: "...party for everyone..."
rewards.driver: The note says: "...with hot chestnuts..."
rewards.receptionist: The note says: "...I am sorry."
rewards.planner: The note is signed by a friend of the town.

objectives.text: Why did the thief take the chestnuts?

rewards.baker: Cellar safety: hot roasting pans must stay away from paper decorations. Restoring trust: the food must be checked before guests eat it.
rewards.shopkeeper: Cellar safety: the moon parcel contains paper lanterns; real flames could burn them. Restoring trust: I want the borrowed key returned.
rewards.driver: Cellar safety: a heavy chestnut sack needs two people to carry it safely. Restoring trust: nobody should carry heavy boxes alone to keep a surprise secret.
rewards.receptionist: Cellar safety: the corridor and both hotel exits must stay clear. Restoring trust: the hotel must know where every delivery is stored.
rewards.planner: Cellar safety: battery lights can replace candles in the lanterns. Restoring trust: a good surprise needs permission and a safe plan.

objectives.text: Write 3 sentences. What happens at the celebration?

Before the celebration, investigate two safety risks. Read your Cellar safety note. Interview your partner about their risk, ask what could happen and suggest a safer alternative. Write a two-item inspection with the evidence, a solution and who should handle it. Useful phrases: "What could go wrong?" "Would it be safer to...?" "Who can take responsibility?"

The chestnuts were taken for a surprise. How can the town rebuild trust? Read your Restoring trust note. Compare the needs of your two roles, propose conditions for continuing the party and negotiate an agreement. Submit two commitments, one thing you changed after listening and how the agreement makes the surprise safer. Useful phrases: "I understand, but we need..." "I could accept that if..." "We agree to..."

discoveries.text: At the hotel there is an old door. It has a lock with four numbers.

reveals.text: News: a neighbor smelled hot chestnuts near the hotel.

chapters.title: The Missing Festival Plan
chapters.intro: The chestnuts are recovered, but the festival plan has vanished. One poster says "park" and another says "hotel". Find the latest plan, check the rehearsal time and agree on a safe place before the party starts at 6:00. Before each conclusion, ask a witness about this question and compare their private evidence with yours in your journal.
chapters.recap: Last time: the chestnuts were in the hotel cellar. Now the town needs a reliable festival plan.
chapters.ending: The latest plan puts rehearsal at 5:30 in the hotel hall. Your safety proposal is ready for the committee. But a strange invitation has arrived, and a ghostly sound comes from the park...

roleClues.shopkeeper: The park poster is an old draft. The red folder contains the signed, latest plan.
roleClues.driver: I delivered a red folder to the hotel, not the park.
roleClues.receptionist: There is a red folder under the guest book on my hotel desk.

objectives.text: Where is the latest festival plan? Name the building.

rewards.shopkeeper: The old poster says rehearsal at 5:00. It is crossed out.

rewards.receptionist: The signed plan says: rehearsal at half past five; party at six.
rewards.planner: The rehearsal starts at 5:30. The party still starts at 6:00.

objectives.text: What time does rehearsal start in the latest plan?

rewards.baker: The food can be served in the hotel hall. The cafe is too small for all the guests.
rewards.shopkeeper: The shop has only one narrow exit. It is not a safe festival room.
rewards.driver: Strong wind is forecast for the park. The hall at the hotel is sheltered.
rewards.receptionist: The hotel hall has two clear exits and enough room for the guests.
rewards.planner: The latest venue must be sheltered and have two clear exits. The park plan is cancelled.

objectives.text: Which building meets the latest safety requirements for the celebration?

rewards.baker: Planning requirement: put the hot food table away from paper lanterns.
rewards.shopkeeper: Planning requirement: use battery lights; no flames inside paper lanterns.
rewards.driver: Planning requirement: leave a clear route from the delivery door to the food table.
rewards.receptionist: Planning requirement: keep both hotel exits clear.
rewards.planner: Planning requirement: include a welcome space for ten new neighbors and start the party at 6:00.

objectives.text: Write a proposal for the festival committee. State the venue and rehearsal time, explain two safety arrangements, and name a decision you would discuss with another role. Use your planning requirement and the available clues.

rewards.baker: Poster review: my food list says hotel hall, rehearsal 5:30, party 6:00. Space negotiation: I need a food table away from lanterns.

rewards.driver: Poster review: the delivery note confirms hotel hall at 5:15. Space negotiation: the delivery route cannot cross a queue.
rewards.receptionist: Poster review: the hotel booking confirms rehearsal at 5:30. Space negotiation: neither exit can have a table or a queue in front of it.
rewards.planner: Poster review: my signed plan cancels the park rehearsal and keeps the 6:00 party. Space negotiation: the welcome space must be easy to find for ten new neighbors.

objectives.text: Two posters disagree. Read your Poster review note and interview your partner about the date, source and times in their record. Useful phrases: "Which version is that?" "Does your record confirm...?" "We should correct..."

Help the committee fit everyone into the hotel hall. Read your Space negotiation note. Explain your needs to your partner, compare two layouts and agree on one compromise that keeps both exits clear. Submit the layout in words, the needs it meets and the compromise each of you made. Useful phrases: "We need space for..." "Could we move...?" "That works if..."

discoveries.text: An old poster says: PARK, REHEARSAL 5:00. Across it someone wrote: OLD DRAFT — CHECK THE RED FOLDER.
Under the guest book: a signed red folder. Latest plan: hotel hall; rehearsal 5:30; party 6:00. Keep both exits clear.

reveals.text: News: the hotel receptionist found the red folder under the guest book.
News: the signed plan confirms rehearsal at half past five and the party at six.
News: wind makes the park unsuitable. The hotel hall has shelter and two exits.

chapters.title: The Haunted Celebration
